source.title: Before the Revelation
source.summary: Debt slavery in pre-Islamic Arabia and how the Quran transformed the creditor-debtor relationship forever.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: In pre-Islamic Arabia, debt was a weapon. A man who couldn't repay could be enslaved, his family taken as collateral, his debt doubled at every missed payment. The practice of riba al-jahiliyyah, literally "the usury of the Age of Ignorance," meant that a borrowed camel could become two, then four, then eight, compounding until the borrower lost everything. When the Quran was revealed, it didn't just ban interest; it declared war on an entire system of financial oppression. This episode traces the debt practices of pre-Islamic Arabia, the revolutionary changes introduced by the Quran and Sunnah, and how the Prophet Muhammad personally forgave debts and taught that relieving a debtor's burden was among the noblest acts a Muslim could perform.

linkedin.post: In pre-Islamic Arabia, debt was more than a financial obligation — it was a path to slavery. A man who borrowed a camel and couldn't repay would see his debt double, then quadruple, then multiply again. The practice of riba al-jahiliyyah, literally "the usury of the Age of Ignorance," meant that missed payments could cost you your family's freedom. Children became collateral. Entire households were enslaved for debts that grew beyond any possibility of repayment. When the Quran was revealed, it didn't just prohibit interest — it dismantled a system of financial oppression that had trapped generations in cycles of bondage. This transformation of the creditor-debtor relationship remains one of Islam's most revolutionary economic contributions. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-wd-1

Your family became collateral. Your children could be enslaved. The Arabs called it riba al-jahiliyyah — the usury of the Age of Ignorance. When the Quran was revealed, it didn't just ban interest.
